value.title: Finite-auxiliary Marton superadditivity and Fekete foundation
value.summary: For the half-skew BSSC, finite auxiliary laws give 0≤M_n^fin(P)≤2n. Concatenating epsilon-optimal finite laws proves M_{m+n}^fin(P)≥M_m^fin(P)+M_n^fin(P), so Fekete's lemma yields lim_n M_n^fin(P)/n=sup_n M_n^fin(P)/n. For any selected finite n-letter law of value S_n, k independent copies have value exactly kS_n; this is an identity for the selected laws, not additivity of the suprema.

value.title: Conditional finite-super-symbol Marton reduction
value.summary: Assuming the stated finite-DMBC private-message Marton achievability theorem (H-Marton), an epsilon-optimal finite n-letter Marton law can be used on the super-channel P^×n and flattened into an ordinary BSSC code. This proves C_sum(P)≥M_n^fin(P)/n for every n and hence the Fekete-limit lower bound. It supplies no fixed-blocklength capacity converse.

value.title: Exact BSSC randomized-time-division maximization
value.summary: Symmetrization reduces the half-skew BSSC randomized-time-division value to J(1/2)+(1/2)max_q D(q), where J(q)=h_2(q/2)-q and D(q)=J(q)-J(1-q). Differentiation and the stationary polynomial 15q^2-15q+2 identify the global maximizer q_-=(15-sqrt(105))/30 and give the accepted closed form for L_RTD.

value.title: Directed exact-RTD interval certificate
value.summary: A dependency-free standard-library verifier brackets sqrt(105) by exact rational square comparisons and evaluates the closed form with outward-rounded high-precision Decimal arithmetic. It certifies 0.3616428844219546156634415781505870072079810107238605552037137298028007<L_RTD<0.3616428844219546156634415781505870072079810107238605552037137298028008 and the corresponding strict doubled interval ending in 56014 and 56016.

value.title: Finite-auxiliary multiletter Marton foundation and RTD threshold
value.summary: The finite-auxiliary Marton sequence is bounded and superadditive and therefore has the stated Fekete limit, while independent repetition scales every selected law exactly. Under H-Marton, its normalized values are achievable BSSC sum-rate lower bounds. The exact RTD value is attained at q_-=(15-sqrt(105))/30 and has the certified strict intervals. Under H-binary, M_1^fin(P)=L_RTD. Under H-Marton, a selected finite n-letter law improves the governed RTD lower bound exactly when S_n>nL_RTD; under both hypotheses this is equivalently improvement over the complete one-letter Marton optimum. No fixed-n equality is asserted as a capacity converse.

placementAudit.rationale: The accepted result establishes finite-auxiliary foundations, super-symbol normalization, and the exact gain threshold for the continuing objective of determining whether multiletter Marton coding improves the BSSC achievable sum rate. Its independent-copy and correlation-structure implications fit the active conditional-product and correlation-pruning thread.
